sent_to_model:
I'm a mom with two grown sons and I also teach preschool. I'd like help writing a reply in an online discussion about deciding whether to have children. I respect people who give that decision a lot of thought, and I want to share how unpredictable raising our boys has been, including how much it helps to laugh. One commenter argues that a parent provides better care than anyone else; I'd like to answer using my work experience. I want to talk about trusting kids as they grow up, and why money and emotional energy both mattered in our decision to stop at two. Our sons have turned out well, but there were certainly some worrying moments along the way. I want to encourage them to consider unexpected costs and limits on emotional resources.

- I work as a preschool teacher and am a mother.
- My father grew up without siblings; he described his childhood as lonely.
- Our younger son recently needed wisdom teeth removed; we paid over $2000.
- Older son's 28th birthday was yesterday; younger son's 22nd birthday is next week.
- Dad's mother was divorced and financially comfortable, but not particularly nurturing.
- Both sons are caring, bright and successful.
- Neither son had trouble during his college years.
- Some childcare professionals are deeply committed to their work; financial rewards aren't their motivation.
- Four-hour flight with a three-year-old suffering from diarrhea; needed humor to cope.
- Older son required two separate police-station visits after calls at 2am during high school.
- Younger son's birth nearly coincided with his brother's birthday; arrived several days later.
- Expected weaning and potty training to be difficult; both went smoothly.
- Organized sports and middle school proved harder than I'd anticipated.
- My parents taught me the value of keeping a sense of humor.
- Giving parenthood serious consideration shows good judgment, though complete readiness isn't possible.
- Parents and their partners have a uniquely personal commitment to their children.
- Good parenting doesn't prevent every risky choice or frightening incident.
- Eventually parents must allow independence and trust their children to handle it.
- Dad's experience helped convince me to have multiple children; I always intended to stop after two.
- My capacity to give emotional support has limits, just as the household budget does.
- Encourage prospective parents to consider unexpected expenses as well as their emotional capacity.
- Give committed childcare workers credit while acknowledging parents' special devotion.

(About me: mother and preschool teacher. Length: it should come to roughly 250-400 words.)

must_cover: Affirm thoughtful preparation as good judgment while explaining that parenting remains unpredictable.
Humor helps parents cope with difficult experiences.
Draw on the writer's experience as a preschool teacher to acknowledge parents' special personal devotion while giving committed childcare workers credit.
Raising children involves worrying episodes and eventually trusting their independence.
Explain the decision to stop at two and encourage considering unexpected costs and limits on emotional resources.
